note: The elder writes to 'the chosen lady'—and I've always found something tender in this. She's real, she's known, she's loved not because of title but because she holds fast to the truth of Jesus. Love in truth is not sentimental; it's clear-eyed, rooted in who Christ is.
Truth is not fleeting—it remains in us and will be with us forever. In a world that shifts and bends, here is a promise that steadies the soul. The Lord Himself is that truth, and He does not change.

Grace, mercy, peace—the greeting echoes Paul's letters, yet here the elder adds a weighty phrase: 'in truth and love.' It's not blessing poured out carelessly, but blessing rooted in Jesus Christ Himself, the Son of the Father. A grandparent's blessing to a beloved child.

What makes an old pastor's heart rejoice? Watching the young walk in truth—obedient to the Father's command, steady and sure. This is more precious than any other news; the faith is being lived out in the next generation.

The elder says this isn't new, but oh, how we need to hear it afresh. Love one another—it's the heartbeat of the faith, ancient as the beginning, yet we drift from it daily. A simple, hard commandment that costs us everything.

Love isn't feeling; it's obedience. It's walking according to His commandments, not the world's. That narrow road of faith—'walk in it'—takes all our will, all our trust, all our love focused on Christ.

Many deceivers—in every age. They deny that Jesus came in the flesh, that He became human, died, rose again. To deny this is to stand against Christ Himself. We must see with clear eyes: these are not small errors, but the work of the Antichrist spirit.

Watch yourselves—there's a weight here. What we've accomplished in Christ is fragile only if we stop watching, stop holding fast. Our reward is full in Him, but we must not grow careless and drift from truth.
To leave the teaching of Christ is to lose the Father and the Son both. It's not a technicality—it's the whole faith. Remain in Him; abide in His word. That's where the life is.
The elder calls the church to discernment and protection. Don't receive those who bring false teaching into your home. Hospitality is precious, but truth comes first. Love sometimes means saying no.
To welcome a deceiver is to become complicit—you participate in their evil. Sharp words, but true. We are responsible for what we harbor, what we encourage, what we lend our voice to.

Paper and ink won't do for this. The elder longs for face-to-face presence—to see the beloved lady, to speak heart to heart. Even our words in writing fall short of the joy that comes when we gather in Christ.

Readers today hear an echo in this simple closing: we too are 'chosen,' and those loved by Christ greet us in faith. From John's sister church, through the centuries, to us—the communion of the saints continues.
